subject.title: Feature request: config option to suppress transient tool error warnings

question: Should OpenClaw add a normal-chat tool-error delivery policy beyond `messages.suppressToolErrors`, and what safety rule should apply to failed mutating tools after success-looking replies?
rationale: The remaining work changes user-visible failure delivery and config semantics: it improves hosted/team-chat UX but can also hide real failed mutations that current code intentionally surfaces.

options.title: Approve default-compatible policy
options.body: Add a documented `all` default with explicit `final` and/or `off` modes only after regression coverage proves real failed mutations are not silently confirmed.

options.title: Keep the boolean path
options.body: Treat `messages.suppressToolErrors` as the supported operator opt-out and narrow this issue to docs or channel-specific bugs.

options.title: Split remaining leaks first
options.body: Defer the enum and handle narrower Feishu, lifecycle-warning, and read-only probe warning issues separately.

recommendation.title: Approve default-compatible policy
recommendation.body: Add a documented `all` default with explicit `final` and/or `off` modes only after regression coverage proves real failed mutations are not silently confirmed.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the merged warning-policy fix that explicitly scoped this issue as the broader product/config decision.
